producer_report.summary: Queued request commit subjects now take the request's first non-Priority, non-blank line through `plan::title_line`, capped at 60 characters, so a request starting 'Priority: urgent' is titled by its request. The Dropped subject already uses the same helper through `job.title()`, so it needed no change. This turn added the end-to-end test that queues through `Athena::queue` and asserts the commit subject. CHANGELOG.md has the entry.

checks_run.note: Runs the new end-to-end test and the existing helper test; both pass.
Banned-word and policy scan; 17 tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, the `queue` subject uses `crate::plan::title_line(&request.text)` (then the 60-char cap) instead of `lines().next()`; check the diff.
criteria_check.evidence: git diff shows `queue` now calls `queue_subject(&request.text)`, and the helper (reading.rs, near line 1358) is `let line: String = crate::plan::title_line(text).chars().take(60).collect();`. The old `request.text.lines().next()` block is removed.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in reading.rs queues a request whose first line is 'Priority: urgent' followed by a real request line. It asserts the commit subject is 'Queue a request: <real line>' and does not contain 'Priority'. Check with `cargo test -p athena-core` and the test name in the diff.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `a_queued_request_commit_names_the_request_not_its_priority` in reading.rs builds a real repo, calls `athena.queue("Priority: urgent\n\nFix the widget")`, and reads the commit subject with `git log -1 --format=%s`. It asserts equality with 'Queue a request: Fix the widget' and that the subject does not contain 'Priority'. `cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_queued_request` passes. The verifier can run that command.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff shows no raw first-line subject left for a Dropped commit. The Dropped subject path (manage.rs via `job.title()`) is either shown to use `title_line` or changed to use it.
criteria_check.evidence: manage.rs:211 uses `crate::run::closing_subject(state, &job.title())`. store.rs:150-155 (JobRecords::title) calls `crate::plan::title_line`, per the grep I ran. Grep for 'Dropped' in athena-core/src found no raw-first-line subject builder. I did not open all of store.rs. No change was needed.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under the unreleased section saying that queued and dropped request commit subjects skip leading Priority lines.
criteria_check.evidence: git diff CHANGELOG.md adds a bullet under the unreleased section saying queued and dropped request commit subjects skip leading `Priority:` lines and blank lines.

open_issues: Not verified by running: that the new end-to-end test fails on the pre-change source. By inspection, the old `lines().next()` code would give the subject 'Queue a request: Priority: urgent', which fails the assertion. Athena may run this check.
mistakes: My first pass tested only the `queue_subject` helper, not the path through `Athena::queue`, so the new-test criterion was not met. This turn adds the end-to-end test.
I tried to pipe cargo output through `tail`, which the Bash policy rejects. I reran the command without it.
learnings: `Athena::queue` in reading.rs needs a repository with athena.toml and defaults.toml at HEAD. `crate::test_support::make_athena(&git, state, vec![], script)` builds an Athena over it, and `athena.queue` returns (JobId, commit hash).
The shipped athena.toml works unchanged as the config for a queue-only test repository.
The producer Bash policy rejects `tail` and only allows cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm.
